abstract: Non-repudiation and fairness are two important issues in electronic transactions. There is a famous securely fair non-repudiation protocol (SFNRP) proposed by B. Meng that can satisfy these two requirements. However, the bottleneck problem does not be solved completely. In this paper, we propose a new fair non-repudiation protocol, in which the trusted third party (TTP) is off-line to further reduce TTP's involvement and solve the bottleneck problem. By security analyses, the new protocol can greatly improves SFNRP. At the same time, it can provide the protocol privacy and reduce the involvement of TTP.

articleTitle: A novel approach to internet connectivity for mobile ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The existing approaches for providing global Internet connectivity for mobile ad hoc networks often cause low packet delivery ratio and high routing overhead. In this paper, a novel approach to Internet connectivity for mobile ad hoc networks is proposed. This approach bases on Identity/Location split, which separates the location of the host from its identity. Both of the mobile ad hoc network nodes and Internet nodes communicate with each other using their unique identities. The IP address functions only as location. Mobile ad hoc network nodes can easily connect to Internet without understanding of IP addressing and routing within Internet under this approach. This approach has higher packet delivery ratio and lower routing overhead compared to other approaches.

articleTitle: The DAMA of DVB-RCS based broadband satellite communication networks with OBP
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper provides an overview of broadband satellite communication networks based on digital video broadcasting-return channel system (DVB-RCS) standard, with an emphasis on the dynamic assignment multi-access (DAMA) of return channels. An OPNET simulation system is developed to study the QoS performance of several combined DAMA protocols. The satellite onboard processing (OBP) and the self-similar traffic model are considered in the simulation system. Simulation results indicate that adaptive dynamic assignment protocols have better QoS performance, and the characteristics of traffic models will influence the QoS performance significantly.

articleTitle: PERED:A new AQM algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper gives a new active queue management algorithm which creates a dynamical Markov model according to the traffic loads to estimate the future queue size of router buffer and self-adjusts the parameters of well-known Random Early Detection (RED) to get better performance, so we call it Pre-Estimation RED, simply PERED. In PERED we present a new idea to control the congestion in networks: previous estimation. We demonstrate the improvement in performance of PERED by comparison with RED and an adaptive RED.

articleTitle: A human-centered pervasive computing system model
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Pervasive computing is considered as the next generation computing after network computing. It is also considered as the next generation IT technology. For the network technology, OSI Reference Model provides us a general understanding of the computer networks. Such a reference model is very helpful for the network analysis and design issues. Inspired by the OSI Reference Model, we propose a Human-Centered Pervasive Computing System Model (HPC) to facilitate the discussion and analysis of pervasive computing systems. With this model we can easily see the relationships among the pervasive computing components. It helps us to understand some key pervasive computing concepts and technologies.

articleTitle: A decorrelating aided partial combining rake receiver for direct sequence ultra-wideband communication systems
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The performance of direct sequence ultra-wideband (DS-UWB) RAKE reception is severely degraded by interpath interference (IPI), which in general consists of intersymbol interference (ISI) and interchip interference (ICI). Based on similarities between the signals of asynchronous CDMA systems and the signals received by UWB RAKE receivers, especially partial combining RAKE (PRAKE) receiver, decorrelating algorithm is introduced to combat IPI. Sliding window approach is utilized for implementation of the decorrelator. Computer simulations under the channel model proposed by IEEE 802.15.3a verify the effectiveness of the decorrelating scheme.

articleTitle: A design of LDPC codes with large girth based on the sub-matrix shifting
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we present an approach for constructing LDPC codes with girth 8. First, we design 3 submatrices with different shifting functions given by our schemes, then combine them into a matrix according to our approach, finally, expand the matrix into a desired parity-check matrix using identity matrices and cyclic shift matrices of the identity matrices. The simulation results in AWGN channels show that these codes which can be obtained by the generator matrix derived from this check matrix for encoding the random information bits are as good as random LDPC codes.

articleTitle: Decoupled estimation of the central DOA and angular spread for coherently distributed source
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of estimating the parameter — the central directions of arrival (DOA) and angular spread of distributed source by one-dimension searching algorithm based on preliminary estimate of the central DOA. Decoupling the estimation of the central DOA from that of angular spread enable two-step procedure. The preliminary estimate of the central DOA can be obtained at a signal subspace, which downsize searching scope. The proposed algorithm has improved precision, low computational cost and sufficient robustness. Simulations clearly demonstrate that the algorithm is not only effective, but also enjoys better performance compared with DSPE algorithm.

articleTitle: A new classifier combination method based on TSK-type fuzzy system
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a new classifier combination method based on TSK-type fuzzy system. The new method includes linear combination as a special case and it is potential to outperform linear combination by tuning its parameters. The fuzzy system used to combine the classifiers has a good comprehensibility since the number of fuzzy rules is very small. In the new method, first, the parameters of the TSK-type fuzzy system are initialized based on an efficient linear combination method, multi-response linear regression; then, the gradient descendent algorithm is used to tune the parameters. Experimental results on three data sets form the ELENA project database and the UCI database show that the proposed classifier combination method outperforms the multi-response linear regression and other typical classifier combination methods such as voting and multilayer perceptron networks.

articleTitle: Adaptive step-size natural gradient algorithm based on separating degree gradient
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper proposes to use separating degree to control the step-size of natural algorithm for the first time. After detailed analyzing relevant fixed step-size and variable step-size gradient algorithms, the paper presents a new adaptive step-size natural algorithm. Because the variability of the new algorithm's step-size is based on separating degree, its learning ratio is chosen adaptively according to separating degree, therefore it can improve convergence speed and reduce the misadjustment error in the steady state simultaneously. Computer simulations confirm the theoretical analysis and show the algorithm performance is superior to other natural algorithms.

articleTitle: The technology of route optimization for NEMO based on DHCPPD
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The basic NEMO protocol results in a sub-optimal route between Mobile Network Node (MNN) and Correspondent Node (CN). This paper provides a mechanism based on DHCP Prefix Delegation (DHCPPD) to enable Mobile Network Node (MNN) to perform route optimization with CNN which has basic MIPv6 support. The goal is to use DHCPPD to assign Care-Of-Address (COA) to MNN, MNN can bind with Correspondent Node (CN) with basic MIPv6 support [3]. It effectively reduce unnecessary large travelling route and overhead, thereby enhance the performance. The solution is effective for both single NEMO and nested NEMO for which we will deploy DHCP replay mechanism as extension, and has a better performance than the basic NEMO protocol.

articleTitle: A Simplified kalman-MLSD receiver over fast fading channel
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: A new adaptive reduced-complexity Maximum likelihood sequence detection (MLSD) receiver applying reduced-state sequence estimation based on Per-survivor processing (RSSE-PSP) algorithm and decision feedback algorithm (DF) over fast fading mobile channel with 16QAM modulation is proposed in this paper. The adaptive channel tracking is implemented by a simplified kalman filter bank with very short pilot tone. Computer simulations show that this receiver is a good trade-off between the performance and complexity on fast fading mobile channels.

articleTitle: A research of forward neural network blind equalization algorithm based on momentum term
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In order to overcome the influence of iteration step-size to algorithm performance, an improved neural network blind equalization algorithm based on momentum term is proposed in this paper. The simulation shows that the improved algorithm has faster convergence rate and lower bit error rate.

articleTitle: Study on multi-Carrier CDMA systems based on poly-phase Orthogonal sequences
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: MC-CDMA (Multi-Carrier CDMA) is an integrated technology of OFDM (Orthogonal frequency-division multiple access) and CDMA (Code-division multiple access). This technology is considered as the core technology of the future communications, because it keeps the advantages of OFDM and CDMA. The fundamental principles of transmitter and receiver of MC-CDMA are analyzed in the paper firstly. Then MC-CDMA system models are simulated with MALAB. Using poly-phase orthogonal sequence wave as the spread spectrum sequences in MC-CDMA system, original data can be recovered, through the AWGN Channel.

articleTitle: New applications of p-subgroup problems in broadcast encryption services
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we exploit new applications of the p-subgroup problems in broadcast encryption services and present a new traitor tracing scheme based on the extended modified p-subgroup problem. The proposed scheme is provably as secure as large integer factoring problems and has the advantages of fast computation, efficient join and revocation of users. And the proposed black-box tracing algorithm can trace all the traitors contributing to the pirate decoder.

articleTitle: A semi-blind multiuser detection based on a subspace constrained RLS algorithm for MC-CDMA uplink
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, a new semi-blind multiuser detection based on a subspace constrained RLS algorithm is proposed for multicarrier code division multiple access (MC-CDMA) systems. In the MC-CDMA uplink, the base station receiver has the knowledge of the spreading sequences of all the users within the cell, but not that of the users from other cells. By imposing linear vector constraints on the multiuser detector, the proposed semi-blind detection can efficiently suppress the intracell interferers, while mitigating the intercell interferers based on the mean output energy (MOE) principle. A subspace constrained RLS algorithm is proposed to obtain the MOE weight vector adaptively. To reduce the computational complexity, an improved projecting approximation subspace tracking with deflation (PASTd) algorithm is proposed to calculate the signal subspace. Numerical results show that the performance of the proposed semi-blind detector is much better than the RLS-based MOE blind multiuser detection.

articleTitle: A new access control model with authority tracking function in E-commerce
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: With the prevalence of E-commerce, the information security problems are standing out. One critical requirement of security is the accountability and it is worth researching on how to record the information to find out illegal actions. This paper applies the mathematic methodology of graph theory and finite state machine theory to give a new access control model which is able to track the authorizing history based on the “Active Defense Information Security Insurance Technique Frame”. Authority Propagating Tree (APT) is proposed and the security model based on APT is developed. The formal definition, theorem systems and operation rules of the model are illustrated in the paper.

articleTitle: A new multi-channel MAC Protocol with Power Control for Ad hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a new multi-channel MAC Protocol with Power Control for Ad hoc Networks. First, the code channel is divided into common channel, broadcast channel and data channel while code synchronization is dynamically implemented through RTS/CTS handshake. In order to decrease handshake cost and avoid code channel switching frequently, Dual Reservation scheme is proposed through ACK Piggybacking. And furthermore, dynamic power control mechanism is implemented to reduce near-far interference. Besides, broadcast is well supported by an out-of-band busy tone. Compared with IEEE 802.11 DCF protocol, the simulation results show that the proposed mechanism can achieve better performance of network throughput.

articleTitle: Analysis of handoff packet loss rate and handoff serving delay in cdma2000 1xEV-DO Rev A
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In the downlink of cdma2000 1x EV-DO system, virtual soft handoff technology is implemented through sector selection between related sectors, as a result some packets may be lost and data service interrupted during this procedure. This paper analyzes the reasons of packet loss and service delay caused by handoff in detail, and in order to reduce them we presents two ways: allocate appropriate buffer size and improve scheduling algorithm. Simulation results show that lower handoff packet loss rate, smaller handoff service delay and higher downlink data throughput can be obtained through controlling the downlink buffer size in BSs and exploiting handoff-based PF scheduling algorithm.

articleTitle: Proactive worm prevention based on P2P networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: According to the features of worm propagation, a novel model for proactive worm prevention based on peer-to-peer (P2P) networking technologies is proposed in this paper. At first, we present the backgrounds and security issues related to P2P networks. Then, a structured P2P overlay network designed for worm prevention is specified. Based on that, we present the methods for Internet worm forecasting which is assumed to be unknown. Furthermore, we study effective strategies to restrain and eliminate worms under the model. We find that our proposed P2P-based worm prevention model can efficiently reduce the impact of worms on the networks.

articleTitle: A distributed DiffServ supporting scheduling scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The convergence of diverse traffic requires modern networks to provide QoS (Quality of Service) solutions to time-critical applications. Due to its simplicity and scalability, the differentiated service (DiffServ) solution is expected to be widely deployed across the Internet. In this paper, we propose a distributed DiffServ supporting scheduling (DDSS) scheme based on buffered crossbar switches. The schedulers of the proposed DDSS scheme can be implemented on each input and each output independently and in parallel, hence are more practical and scalable. Simulation results show that DDSS scheme can provide minimum bandwidth guarantees for EF and AF traffic and fair bandwidth allocation for BE traffic. DDSS scheme also exhibits good delay performance for EF traffic and AF traffic through simulations.

articleTitle: A new complexity control algorithm for transform and quantization in AVS-M Video encoder
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: AVS-M is a new video standard used for mobile application. The key of applying AVS-M standard is implementation of efficient coding algorithms. An efficient method is to reduce number of computing transform and quantization by determining all zero blocks before do them. However, complexity reductions by existed algorithms vary with different video content and is disadvantageous for fixed frame rate coding. This results in decrease of video continuity and subjective quality. In this paper, a new algorithm for controlling computation complexity is presented. It controls number of blocks need to be transformed and quantized near to a constant by adjusting determination threshold of all zero block detection adaptively. Simulation results show range of complexity change is no more than 3% and algorithm convergence within 24 frames under acceptable video quality.

articleTitle: On the performance of time-hopping M-ary biorthogonal pulse position modulation ultra-wideband communication system
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new modulation scheme called time-hopping (TH) M-ary biorthogonal pulse position modulation (MBPPM) for ultra wideband (UWB) systems with asynchronous multiple-access interference (MAI) in an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). Closed-form expression of symbol error rate (SER) is provided, then the simple expression is obtained for the system. The performances of TH MBPPM and TH M-ary orthogonal PPM (MOPPM) schemes are compared in terms of the SER in the end. It is shown that the TH MBPPM outperforms the TH MOPPM system and half the system complexity for the same values of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the number of users respectively.

articleTitle: Improvement of rate control for JPEG2000 at low bit rate
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: To speed up the encoding process at low bit rate, a improvement of rate control based on the basic idea of PCRD in JPEG2000 is proposed. The aim of the algorithm is to achieve equivalent performance of PCRD with less computational complexity and smaller memory buffer at low bit rate. The main improvement exists where it determines the included coding passes of a code block before they will be encoded. Therefore, the excluded passes will never be encoded actually, which results in the fact that the computational operations and the memory of buffering the temporary bit stream would be reduced greatly. The performance of the proposed method is experimentally investigated in jasper VM software.

articleTitle: An improved LCMV method at subarray level
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: ADBF at subarray level has important applications in phased array radar systems, and this paper studies LCMV methods at subarray level. The limitation of the conventional LCMV at subarray level is that the SLL (SideLobe Level) of the adaptive pattern may remarkably increase. And that LCMV based on normalization and that based on MOD can suppress the SLL well, but bring in biggish IF (Improvement Factor) loss. This paper combines LCMV based on normalization and that based on MOD, which can not only suppress the SLL but reduce IF loss. Simulation results indicate the validity of the introduced method.

articleTitle: A mandarin e-learning system design and implementation based on pervasive computing
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we present the design and implementation for a mandarin e-learning system based on pervasive computing. We apply the Human-centered Pervasive Computing System Model (HPC) and the Layered Architecture Analysis and Design Method (LAAD) to the system design. Based on the HPC model and the LAAD method, a mandarin e-learning system is implemented. The design and implementation issues are discussed in more details.

articleTitle: A robust switching-beam algorithm designed for long range underwater acoustic communication
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The SNR (signal to noise ratio) of the received signal in long range UUV underwater communication system can be increased by using beamforming technology. But owing to the moving of the UUV, a switching-beam algorithm is needed to detect the beam pointing to the DOA of incident signal. The traditional time domain switching-beam (TDSB) algorithm is incapable of tracing the DOA while the SNR of the received signal is low. In order to solve this problem, a frequency domain switching-beam (FDSB) algorithm is proposed. In the proposed algorithm, the beam output is converted into frequency domain by FFT. The beam pointing to the DOA of the incident signal is judged by comparing the peak values of signal spectrums. Computer simulation is done with channel model based on sea test data. The simulation results show that compared with the TDSB algorithm, the proposed FDSB algorithm has better performance when the SNR of the received signal is very low.

articleTitle: Adaptive compressed video steganography in the VLC-domain
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: A novel, low complexity chaotic steganography method applicable to MPEG-2 videos is proposed. The security of this algorithm is based on the randomness of steganography location. One class of perturbed digital chaos is employed to generate pseudo random sequences with perfect statistical properties. In this work, the embedding and detection are both done entirely in the variable length code (VLC) domain, with no need for full or even partial decompression to meet the real-time require ment. Experimental results verify the availability of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Using mobile router chain to support route optimization in IPv6 nested NEMO
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Mobility is an important feature of future internet, and mobility of mobile node in IPv6 has been designed as RFC3775, with optimized route and safeguard of binding messages as its characters. However, as the development of sensor network and personal network, the ability of allowing node and route, which reside in a moving network, to visit internet is imminent for applications in reality. Although some approaches to support network mobility are proposed based on extension of mobile ipv6, resolving the basic routing in mobile networks, nested mobile networks is still confronting serious issues, such as binding updates explosion, triangle route, and source address filtration, resulting. In this paper, we propose an approach to optimize route in IPv6 nested mobile networks by designing mobile router chain, which can be used by mobile and fixed networks and nodes, residing in a mobile network, to analyze the nested topology and improve mobility management in result.

articleTitle: Research and implementation of network processor architecture modeling
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: With the development of network applications, network devices need more intelligent processing capability. network processors (NPs) emerge timely and are widely used in network domains to meet these requirements. Because of the complexity of NP, there are many challenges for design of NP. In this paper, a system design methodology is studied, and based on SystemC. a platform used to model network processor architecture is constructed. This platform is composed of an extensible heterogeneous resource library and an architecture constructor. The former provides user some common resource model. The latter can automatically generate model instance from a configuration table provided by designers. This modeling methodology and platform is general which could be used to construct various network processor architecture models in short time.

articleTitle: A random geometric graph coverage model of wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: A new random geometric graph coverage model is presented in this article. Compared with other old simple models, this new model considers not only the sensitivity of node but also the reliability of links. It is more appropriate to real situations, affected by various factors. The model shows its applicability when all wireless sensor networks' (WSN) nodes obtaining its own coordinate for coverage and surveillance purposes. We also analyze some key parameters of WSN as a new model of random geometric graph and propose a simple greedy localization algorithm. In the end, empirical results demonstrate the validity of proposed model and algorithm.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of real-time processing system in underwater acoustic communication
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication real-time processing system, which plays an important role in AUV, realizes real-time processing of data and output of control instruction. ADSP-TS101 is a high performance DSP with good performance of parallel processing and high speed. A real-time processing system composed with multiple ADSP-TS101s and multi-channel synchronous sampling was designed and carried out. FPGA logical control was adopted for hardware design of multi-channel synchronous sampling module, and cluster/data flow associated pin connection mode was adopted for multiprocessing parallel processing configuration. The software was optimised by tow hardware communication ways, which were broadcast-write through the shared parallel bus and point-to-point through link ports. From the whole system installation, debugging, and experiments conducted in a lake, the results show that the real-time processing system satisfies the engineering requirements and has good stability and real-time processing capability.

articleTitle: An video watermarking algorithm based on wavelet domain
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, an video watermarking algorithm that based on wavelet domain is proposed. In order to enhance the robustness of the watermark, we propose to classify the wavelet coefficients based on the motion of the objects and the texture complexity of the contents in the video sequence. According to the result of classification and the correlation of frames, the watermark is adjusted adaptively and inserted into the coefficients of the wavelet transform low-frequency subband. The experimental results show that the proposed watermarking algorithm has good robustness to video degradation and distortion.

articleTitle: A novel spread spectrum OFDM underwater acoustic communication
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Spread spectrum methods are used in underwater acoustic communication (UAC) systems to provide robust acoustic links or long distance communication abilities. However, the bandwidths of ocean channels limit the data rate of spread spectrum UAC. The method using quasi-orthogonal sequences with phase shift keying and parallel transmission to increase the data rate of spread spectrum UAC can be found in Refs.1and 2. In this paper, we apply OFDM to realize parallel transmission of spread spectrum signal. Firstly, spread spectrum OFDM (SS-OFDM) is introduced into UAC. Then, a novel SS-OFDM method named MSS-OFDM based on M-ary quasi-orthogonal sequences is proposed in this paper. The processing gain of SS-OFDM is 10 * log <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> (L), where L is the length of PN sequence used in SS-OFDM. The bit error rate (BER) performance of SS-OFDM and MSS-OFDM compare to OFDM is analyzed and simulated in AWGN channel. Computer simulation results using multi-path channel model based on lake test data show that MSS-OFDM has double anti-multipath abilities, which can significantly improve the data rate of spread spectrum UAC with a robust performance, even without cycle prefix. Water tank experiments were conducted to check this novel method. Simulation and test results show that MSS-OFDM can provide robust and moderate high-speed spread spectrum UWA communication.

articleTitle: Complementary spreading CDMA systems under electrical and multipath interferences
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The BER performance of presented CDMA systems will rapidly deteriorate under the conditions of strong electrical and multipath interferences. To solve the problem, this paper develops a complementary spreading CDMA (CS-CDMA) system with complementary codes. Different from the classical CDMA systems, the base station of CS-CDMA assigns complementary spreading codes for every mobile stations, the mobile station despreads the data flow by two complementary matching filters. The mobile receiver will curb the effects of strong electrical interference and multipaths interference by their complementary characteristics of cross-correlation, so the system performances (BER and SINR) can be improved much. Since presented complementary spreading codes cannot exhibit good BER performance for the strong interference, this paper develop a new kind quasi-complementary spreading codes. The paper analyzes the performance of complementary spreading CDMA systems theoretically and experimentally for under such electrical and multipath conditions. The simulation results show the good BER performance of the proposed CS-CDMA scheme.

articleTitle: TL-RED: A traffic load adaptive RED algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: TCP combined with Active Queue Management algorithm is the primary solution of the congestion control problem of IP network. RED is the famous AQM algorithm but it cannot performs well when traffic load is heavy and when the traffic load changes for the reason that the congestion notification sending rate of RED algorithm is determined by max<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> and the value of max<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> is fixed. As a result, it will lead to queue size oscillation, which results in queuing delay and jitter. This paper proposes a new adaptive AQM algorithm named TL-RED (Traffic Load adaptive RED). Our goal is to stabilized the queue size in a wide variety of traffic scenarios. TL-RED can adjust the value of max<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> to the changes of the traffic load so that the congestion notification can be sent to sufficient TCP sources to mitigate the congestion level. Simulation results indicate that TL-RED can effectively avoid the queue overflow and stabilize the queue occupation independent of the number of active TCP connections thus resulting in a more predictable packet delay in the network.

articleTitle: A new ID-based blind signature from bilinear pairings
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The blind signature scheme is a protocol for obtaining a signature from a signer, but the signer is unable to view the contents of the message he signs. It is very important technologies in secure e-commerce. Recently the bilinear pairing such as Weil or Tate pairing on elliptic curves and hyperelliptic curves has been found various applications in cryptography. Several ID-based cryptosystems using bilinear pairings were presented. ID-based public key cryptosystem can be a good choice for certificate-based public key infrastructures, especially when efficient key management and moderate security are required. This paper presents a new ID-based blind signature scheme from bilinear pairings. Also we analyze their efficiency and security. The proposed scheme is more efficient than Zhang and Kim's scheme in [8].

articleTitle: Policy-based distributed management for wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Wireless sensor network is a revolution of information sensing and collecting, where the sensor nodes communicate via multi-hop wireless links. The task of management of Wireless sensor networks in environments with hundreds and thousands of sensor nodes is significantly more challenging than stationary and wired networks. In this paper, we present the distributed management architecture of wireless sensor networks on the basis of introduction on particular requirement for its management, to facilitate adaptive and autonomous management of wireless sensor networks. Then the mechanism and characteristics of wireless sensor network management are analysed. The study shows that the management architecture of wireless sensor networks should adapt to the peculiarities of dynamic network topology, limited battery power and constrained wireless bandwidth. The capability of the distributed management is scalable to accommodate the number and heterogeneity of nodes, autonomous and survivable to adapt to network dynamics, and economical to minimize management overhead.

articleTitle: A new RFIC receiver structure for cognitive radio
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, a new RFIC receiver architecture for cognitive radio is proposed, which consists of up-mixer and down-mixer. This architecture alleviates the design of on-chip VCO. This solution can satisfy the design of US television spectrum between 54MHz and 862MHz, and extend to 1668MHz. That means this up-down structure can support cognitive radio (or software radio) application which frequency is between 54MHz and 1668MHz.

articleTitle: A mechanism to control free-riding in P2P networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The phenomenon of free-riding (users consuming network resources without providing resources to the network) is common in peer-to-peer (P2P) systems. In the ideal case, P2P networks will exhibit both non-excludability and non-rivalry. And a recent research showed that P2P networks could operate effectively in the presence of significant free-riding. However, in the presence of free-riding, P2P networks will exhibit levels of rivalry. Many researchers have attempted to prevent the free-riding in P2P networks. In the paper, we propose a mechanism to control the free-riding, not to prevent. One peer does not control the free-riding until its traffic is close to overload in the mechanism. The mechanism can make users (including free-riding) share files easily and sustain the performance of system at the same time.

articleTitle: OCSMA/CA: A MAC protocol to support OFDMA in wireless LAN
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Orthogonal Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance (OCSMA/CA), a novel Medium Access Control (MAC) protocol to support Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA) in Wireless LAN (WLAN), is presented in this paper. In OCSMA/CA, subcarrier state information is transmitted with Request-To-Send (RTS) and Clear-To-Send (CTS) packets before data transmission, so adaptive subcarrier allocation can be performed based on a proposed Virtual Subcarrier Sense (VSS) mechanism. In this scheme, each node has a standard Network Allocation Vector (NAV) and an additional Subcarrier Allocation Vector (SAV). Simulation results show that OCSMA/CA can support OFDMA effectively and can significantly increase the network throughput.

articleTitle: Objective video quality assessment for mobile application
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, the objective video quality assessment has been used to the mobile application. We propose a set of objective video quality assessment model to evaluate the video transmission quality over a wireless channel. By this way, we can rate the quality of the multimedia wireless transmission more objectively and economically. This objective video quality assessment model can be sensible to most of the usual video distortion and have good correlation with the subjective assessment.

articleTitle: Analyse of the application schemes for the wireless network security
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The wireless network is the fast developed wireless data communication technology in recent years. Its security performance has become one of the key performance of the wireless network. In this paper, we have analysed several kinds of wireless network security precaution measures, provided the wireless network security suggestion. And finally we presented several application schemes of the wireless network security under three kinds of different environments.

articleTitle: The DOA tracking method based Gaussian particle filter in smart antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Direction Of Arrival (DOA) tracking is an important section of Space Division Multiple Access (SDMA) and beam forming in smart antennas. Because of quickly moving of CDMA users, and many users operate the same frequency at one time, and there are some coherent signals which propagation in space through multi-path, general analytical approaches are difficult to handle the problem. This paper proposed a new method based Gaussian particle filter, which performance is asymptotic optimal that tend to MMSE, it demand only a few snapshots for obtaining DOA parameters, and can tracking multi-targets which be coherent or not. The simulation has been performed to indicated that the new method can be applied in facility.

articleTitle: Approach based on ICA and GCA to identify field mixed acoustic objects
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: With independent component analysis (ICA) to realize the blind separation from mixed acoustic objects, an identification method based on gray correlation analysis (GCA) is proposed through extracting linear prediction coefficient (LPC) feature. It is revealed that LPC is consistently better than wavelet energy feature, ICA is efficient algorithm to estimate the unknown signal level and GCA may reflect the difference and similarity of the influences of factors or characteristics effectively. The validity of the new methods is verified via examples in mixed acoustic objects identification system.

articleTitle: A joint data link layer and network layer design for cluster-based wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: To improve the performance of wireless sensor networks, there has been increased interest in network protocols that rely on cross-layer design recently. In this paper, we present a cross-layer method for cluster-based wireless sensor networks to provide energy efficiency and low latency. In the proposed approach, the adaptive cluster head selection scheme and the cluster route scheme can eliminate the idle listening and collisions to improve power efficiency and reduce transmission latency. Simulation results show the improvement of the network performance by using the joint design.

articleTitle: Password-based key retrieval protocol for roaming systems
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, a new password-based key retrieval protocol for roaming systems is presented. A roaming user can download his secret key from a group of servers only with his identity and a simple password by this protocol. Different from previous protocols, the presented protocol is very efficient not only when servers are well but also when some servers are compromised. In addition, because a new technique is adopted, the presented protocol has a unique attribute, that is, it can detect the bad servers during execution. It is especially useful where the servers are easy to be compromised. Finally, we give the full performance and security analysis.

articleTitle: An efficient decoder for turbo product codes built using two-error-correcting eBCH codes
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to reduce the number of test patterns (TPs) decoded in the Chase II algorithm when turbo-decoding product codes are constructed with two-error-correcting extended Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocqenghem (eBCH) codes. We classify TPs by their values and the relationship of syndromes, and then reject those TPs that have the same codeword. The method needs not to check whether errors are located at the least reliable bits (LRBs) positions to ensure that there are no same codewords decoded. For two-error-correcting eBCH (64,51,2), the simulation results show that over 50% TPs need not be decoded for moderate signal to noise ratios (SNRs) without any decoding performance loss.

articleTitle: A study on direct-up conversion transmitter architecture for WCDMA handset
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper presents a direct-up conversion transmitter (DCT) architecture scheme, which satisfies the requirements of the 3G WCDMA mobile phone system based on 3GPP technique specifications. Firstly, the DCT architecture for WCDMA handset is evaluated and analyzed in detail. Then, the key problems of DCT, which is implemented in WCDMA systems, are analyzed and simulated with the tool of ADS software, and also the solutions or rather design considerations on these problems are given, then. From the studies above, some useful results for future studies and designs have been achieved. Finally, the prospect of direct-up conversion architecture is given boldly.

articleTitle: Interactive buffer sizing for core routers
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: At present, buffer sizing for routers is generally based on the model of Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) on the transmission layer, ignoring the interaction of the network elements and having its connate limitation as for analyzing the performance for the routers on the network layer. How the routers interact in the network and how can we design the routers practically? From the perspective of the network layer, a new model, introducing the effects brought by each router, is proposed for a TCP link. By comparing the impact of access routers with the impact of core routers on link performance and analyzing the part of core routers with the separate method, a lower bound of required buffer size for an interface of a core router is deduced under given constraints on the maximum loss rate and minimum effective utilization. The simulation results validate the conclusion and also indicate this lower bound for buffer size is much looser than the actual lower bound. Our conclusion is a valuable instruction for practically designing buffer size for core routers.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of IMS based on NS2
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Following a brief overview of the research of “Mobile Service Test Platform”-MSTP- supported by “211 project” of China whose objective is to study Next Generation Network technologies, an analysis of the 3GPP IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) function is provided. Then an introduction of implementing IMS on Network Simulator 2 is given based on MSTP. Finally, we describe the scenario of subscribers communication based on the IMS simulation.

articleTitle: A novel cooperative routing algorithm based on cross-layer relay selection
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Cooperative routing technology can achieve distinct performance gain by selecting suitable relays to forward data. Latency is a important performance of MANET. In this paper, we propose a novel cooperative routing algorithm based on relay selection strategy, where the broadcasting routing packets on potential relays are exploited to collect the channel state information (CSI). Then a distributed algorithm is taken to select the “best” relay from a set of potential relays with which a cooperative routing protocol is presented for Ad Hoc networks. In layered wireless networks, the implementation of relay selection involves time synchronization and cross-layer optimization. The simulative results show that the proposed algorithm outgoes non-cooperative DSDV routing protocol with considerable gain of deliver ratio and latency at the price of acceptable routing load.

articleTitle: The transmission capacity of Hierarchical Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we study some transmission capacity theories of Hierarchical Wireless Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (H-MANET). Firstly, we present the structural protocol model, node's mobility tracking model of H-MANET. Secondly, we propose and prove a critical inequality of transmission capacity of H-MANET. Lastly, we propose and prove a gradual probabilistic quality and the specific expression of expectant availability of transmission capacity of H-MANET. The results enrich the theory of [1] and the information theory of wireless networks in certain degree.

Author Keywords: Hierarchical Wireless Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (H-MANT)

articleTitle: Power de-rating reduction for DFT-S-OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Single-carrier transmission has been accepted for the E-UTRA uplink transmission scheme [1]. Frequency-domain generation of the single-carrier signal, which is called as DFT-spread OFDM, is a current assumption in SC-FDMA radio access since it achieves high commonality in parameter design to OFDM-based radio access in the downlink. DFT-S-OFDM allows for further power de-rating reduction. Spectrum shaping filtering can be used to further reduce the power de-rating of DFT-S-OFDM in frequency domain processing. Another candidate for power de-rating reduction is the FFT input pre-processing technique. In this paper, we give comparison of PAPR/CM performance of the two algorithms for power de-rating reduction, and also discuss the bit-error-rate (BER) influences of the two algorithms.

articleTitle: Adaptive clock recovery for CBR traffic under static-priority scheduling
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Adaptive clock recovery (ACR) method is often used for transporting CBR traffic in packet switched networks. How to deal with the random delay of CBR packet when using ACR method is a remarkable difficulty. For the random delay is mostly caused by queuing in the intermediate node, we modeled the queuing delay of CBR packet induced by transporting through an intermediate node with static priority. We also propose the corresponding source clock parameter estimation method called CoUD (center of uniform distribution) in this paper, and simulation results show that our CoUD outperforms traditional LS (least square) method significantly.

articleTitle: Digital watermarking scheme for color image based on image fusion
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper provides a novel digital watermarking scheme for color image, watermarking image was embedded into the corresponding wavelet coefficients of the original image's R, G, B subimages via discrete wavelet transform. The availability of the extracted watermark is evaluated by comparing the normalized correlation coefficients of the extracted watermark with the original one. Experiment results show high robustness of our approach to the common image processing technique such as JPEG compression and additive noise etc.

articleTitle: Research on smart antenna for inter-satellites laser communication
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Free-space optical communications for inter-satellite links and deep space missions offer significant advantages in comparison to alternate microwave systems. The advantages include: high speed; high bandwidth; small antenna size; narrow field of view; and narrow antenna beam. Simultaneously, the complexity of space communications systems is growing rapidly with the increase in transmission requirements. Most important technology is optical antenna in this communication system. This paper proposes a novel smart antenna for inter-satellites laser communication. The different performances including antenna gain and pattern of optical antenna and smart antenna in inter-satellites laser communication system are given in this paper. The analyse results show that smart antenna is better than optical antenna in this communication system.

articleTitle: Unsupervised texture segmentation based on multi-scale Local Binary Patterns and FCMs clustering
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: This paper present an efficient multi-scale approach to unsupervised texture segmentation based on features extracted from Local Binary Pattern (LBP) histograms and fuzzy C-Means clustering with spatial information. In the approach, a multi-scale version of LBP is firstly adopted to overcome the region limitation of basic LBP by extending to larger scales for texture-content extractions. Texture features consisting of averaged intensities, LBP histogram distributions at different scales are then computed within preset windows. Finally, a modified fuzzy C-Means clustering is performed for small region-based segmentation where the spatial position is involved in the object function for enhancing the spatial-dependency among feature vectors within a texture class. The performance of the proposed method is demonstrated on segmentation of several multi-textured images and comparison studies on feature selection analysis are shown on its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Comparison of pre-FFT and post-FFT beamforming in wireless LANs
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, performance of the pre- and post-FFT beamforming schemes are investigated based on the IEEE 802.11g WLAN indoor channel model. A multi-cluster space-time channel with “Bell” shape Doppler power spectrum is used in the simulation to compare the performance between the two different schemes. Two beamforming algorithms, the DOA-based and the dominant-eigenvector-based, are considered in the WLAN OFDM systems for each scheme.

articleTitle: A fast generalized complex sphere decoder for MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: A fast generalized complex sphere decoder (GCSD) is proposed in this paper. This GCSD can be used to solve the under-determined MIMO systems. Moreover, it can handle not only the QAM and PSK constellations, but also the arbitrary complex constellations. The basic idea is to partition the transmitted signal vector into two sub-vectors. After some transformations, we can use a search scheme which is similar to sphere decoding and a conventional complex sphere decoder to solve these two sub-vectors respectively. Simulation results show that the complexity of our GSCD is significantly lower than the exhaustive search scheme on the under-determined part of the transmitted signal vectors.

articleTitle: A scalable routing protocol for low energy Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The recent interest in Wireless Sensor Networks has led to a number of routing mechanisms that use the limited energy available at sensors more efficiently. In this article, we present a scalable routing protocol for low energy wireless sensor networks. Our routing protocol is based on clustering network topology, which reduces the routing overhead efficiently and makes the scalable networks possible. To maximize network lifetime, we propose energy efficient algorithms in the wireless temperature sensor network platform. Experiment results indicate that performances of this routing protocol satisfy all the parameters in super low energy wireless sensor networks.

articleTitle: Layer extrinsic information transferring (LEXIT) detection algorithm for diversity MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: A new detection algorithm, namely layer extrinsic information transferring (LEXIT) detection algorithm, is proposed for diversity multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) systems. In the LEXIT detection, soft component detection at each receiving time slot is carried out and soft extrinsic information about the transmitted symbol is transferred and updated among different time slots. Simulation results show that the bit error rate (BER) performance of LEXIT is better than that of the soft combining scheme, comparable to the performance of minimum mean square estimation (MMSE) detection. Further, complexity analysis proves that the linear complexity of LEXIT brings the low complexity advantage over that of MMSE, which is the cubic complexity in the number of symbols in one transmission block.

articleTitle: Study of channel allocation in downlink distributed wireless communication system
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we present a simple and efficient method on channel allocation in downlink distributed wireless communication system (DWCS). The analysis and results show that based on this method DWCS significantly outperforms conventional cellular systems in channel capacity. It overcomes the drawback of the cellular system's lower performance of cell boundary users and the channel capacity is increased with higher antennas density.

articleTitle: An improved PEG construction of irregular LDPC codes by conditioning low-degree nodes
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Progressive Edge-Growth (PEG) algorithm is an important approach to construct good LDPC codes at short block lengths. PEG construction with optimized symbol-node degree distributions yield irregular codes with very good performance, especially in the water-fall region. In this paper, we present a modification to the PEG algorithm by conditioning low-degree symbol nodes in the Tanner graph. Our modified algorithm yields irregular codes with improved girth histogram at low-degree symbol nodes. Simulation results show that the modified algorithm can lower the error floor of irregular PEG codes considerably, while having slightly better performance in the water-fall region.

articleTitle: A study on the solution of the CDMA1X wireless data private network
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: CDMA1X wireless data private network is characterized by high speed, wide band, safe and stable. The users do not restrict by time and territory to fulfill wireless telecommunication at any time and place for special requirement of special industry. In the paper, we deeply study the CDMA1X wireless data private network, roundly analyse the solutions of the wireless private network such as Access VPN, L2TP, VR + Private wire and so on, and do some instructive explore in the CDMA1X wireless data private network for its deeply development and application.

articleTitle: A framework for optimization in multi-channel multi-radio wireless mesh networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Multi-hop infrastructure wireless mesh networks offer increased reliability, coverage and reduced equipment costs over their single-hop counterpart, wireless LANs. Equipping wireless routers with multiple radios further improves the capacity by transmitting over multiple radios simultaneously using orthogonal channels. However, due to the limited number of available orthogonal channels, interference is still a factor in such networks. In this paper, we propose a network model that captures the key practical aspects of such systems and characterize the constraints binding their behavior. We mathematically formulate the optimization framework, taking into account the interference constraints, the number of channels in the network and the number of radios available at each mesh router etc. We then use this framework to develop solutions for multiple objectives subject to different kind of fairness constraints on allocation of scarce wireless capacity among mobile clients. The methods proposed in this paper can be a valuable tool for network designers in planning network deployment and for optimizing different performance objectives.

articleTitle: Hierarchical spectrum sharing in cognitive radio communications
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, according to the interference temperature model and channel conditions, we classify available bands, on which cognitive radios are capable of sharing with legacy systems, into two types — TYPE I used for direct communication between cognitive radio service access point (CR-SAP) and cognitive radio base station (CR-BS), and TYPE II used for direct communication between CR-SAP and its neighbor CR-SAPs. We name this classification as hierarchical spectrum sharing (HSS) and propose an identification process. Four kinds of communication scheme are designed based on HSS so that the cognitive radio can adapt to different transmission requirements. Numerical results show that HSS provides a considerable extension to available bands so that the spectral utility may be improved further.

articleTitle: Secure image encryption technique based on multiple Fresnel diffraction transforms
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new secure image encryption algorithm based on the multiple Fresnel diffraction transforms (MFDTs). First, we discuss the properties of MFDTs in detail and conclude that the MFDTs are strongly affected by the diffraction distances. Next, we design a series of diffraction distances as the encryption keys to enhance the security of encryption algorithm. Numerical experiments show that the MFDTs depend strongly on the diffraction distances, the decryption can proceed when the all keys are correct, and the algorithm is robust to the attacks, such as JPEG lossy compressing, cropping, superposing noise, and resampling from the screen copy. Since there is no simple “one-to-one” relationship between the plain text and cipher text in the MFDTs, it is extremely difficult to decrypt the keys with the exhaust research method, the optical scanning method, and the known-plaintext phase retrieval algorithm. Therefore, the encryption algorithm has a higher level of security.

articleTitle: Investigation on umbrella-shape printed dipole
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: When studying an umbrella-shape printed dipole radiating element, matching of balun is significant to element's characteristics of resonance and standing wave. We try to analyze it with the method analyzing circuit in stead of traditional method, Electronic Field Integrated Equation (EFIE). This paper analyzes S parameter of balun, and then investigates the VSWR. With a great deal of simulation by 3D EM simulation software, HFSS, the method analyzing circuit is effective for studying umbrella-shape printed dipole radiating element. In addition, we give the VSWR and radiation pattern of element and array.

articleTitle: Study and performance simulation analysis of OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: There exist severe problems in wireless communication systems, such as frequency selective fading, fast fading and slow fading, all sorts of noise interference and ICI result of multi-path fading. To tackle the problems, many new techniques have been on the way of research. OFDM is one of them. This paper has investigated this technique in great detail. In combined with digital communication technique and the typical model of OFDM system, it has designed and simulated an artificial base-band OFDM system to analysis its function, and the results of simulation is given in the end.

articleTitle: A secure elliptic curve communication scheme for the cluster-based ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Near Term Digital Radio (NTDR) networks, which follow the cluster based design principles, are developed specifically to use in ad hoc settings. A major challenge in the design of these networks is their vulnerability to security attacks, due to unreliable wireless media, host mobility and lack of infrastructure. In this paper, we propose an elliptic curve secure communication scheme for NTDR networks. Specially, an authentication mechanism for a mobile node joining into cluster is introduced. Additionally, End-to-end secure communication and group secure communication in NTDR networks are also described. The security of our proposed scheme is guaranteed by the conjecture that solving the Elliptic Curve Computational Diffie-Hellman Problem (ECCDHP) is intractable.

articleTitle: A new approach to bitstream extraction in H.264 SVC
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Scalable Video Coding is a hot spot in video coding area. JVT is now working on SVC as an annex of the H.264/AVC. One important application of SVC is to deal with various networks conditions using its scalability. But due to the structure of the SVC bitstream and its extraction method, the resolution can only change from higher to lower resolutions, and not vice versa, unless each key frame of GOP was coded as I frame. It causes the dropping of coding efficiency. We present a new approach to bitstream extraction, which extracts all layers for each key frame, so the resolutions can change bidirectional while remains the coding efficiency.

articleTitle: A 5-GHz low phase noise CMOS VCO for IEEE 802.11a WLAN
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: A fully integrated 5.3 GHz low phase noise CMOS VCO for WLAN application was presented and simulated. Based on the analysis of the phase noise theory, a p-tail complementary cross-coupled pairs structure was adopted, and a high performance inductor and the AMOS varactor were designed. Through the simulation in 0.18µm CMOS TSMC technology, the phase noise achieved is −120 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from the carrier frequency. The supply voltage is 1.8 V, and the power dissipation is 5.2 mW, while the tuning range is about 18%. The performance of the proposed VCO well achieves the requirements of the IEEE 802.11a standard.

articleTitle: A smoothing variable step size algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, both Long Range Dependence (LRD) and burstiness are illustrated to show traffic characteristics of original frame sequence can be represented by traffic on the time scale of GOP. A new smoothing variable step size adaptive (S-VSSA) algorithm is presented based on fix step size adaptive (FSSA) algorithm and variable step size adaptive (VSSA) algorithm, which are used to predict MPEG-4 video traffic on large time scale of GOP. And S-VSSA algorithm can improve performance of prediction significantly according to a number of simulations. The new algorithm can achieve fast convergence and small prediction error.

articleTitle: Sparse strategy of sample labelling for feedback in content based image retrieval
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In content-based image retrieval, the retrieval performance heavily depends on two related aspects: the description of image content, and the distance function applied for sorting. In this paper, to bridge the gap between the low level visual feature and the higher semantic concept, a modified pseudo semantic model based on ensemble learning is first built for the effective description of the image content. In each round of feedback, the sparse strategy of sample labelling is exploited, thus those most informative samples can be provided to the user for labelling, which makes the subsequent online learning abilities improved for next round of feedback, i.e. the learned classifier can take on stronger generalities.

articleTitle: Cluster-based routing with backup route in mobile ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Effective routing is critical in mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs). In recent years, many hierarchical routing protocols have been proposed to build a backbone structure for supporting MANET routing, especially for large scalability. The clustering approach is seen as the first step in providing a flat network with a hierarchical architecture. The clusterheads become the backbone nodes (BNs), which use greater power to transmit packets, forming the backbone network. Backbone network routing can reduce the number of data-packet forwarding hops throughout the entire network. However, previous protocols have focused on clustering schemes. Fault tolerance in a backbone structure has not been considered. In this paper, we propose a backup routing scheme that can repair broken links locally without activating a route re-discovery procedure. The backup route is piggybacked in the data packet header to achieve the most durable route. The proposed method can improve the packet delivery ratio and reduce control overhead, compared to general hierarchical routing protocols.

articleTitle: A hybrid MIMO detector combining SIC and PIC based on wideband MIMO channels
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: VBLAST is the famous layered space-time signal processing algorithm, the original research of VBLAST assumes that channel fading is flat. The detection process of VBLAST uses linear combination nulling and successive symbol cancellation based on inversing and ordering. The high delay of processing is the major disadvantage of the scheme. This paper, we develop a hybrid MIMO detector applying of successive interference cancellation (SIC) and parallel interference cancellation (PIC) based on wideband MIMO channels. The scheme employs SIC algorithm at first slayer detector based on MMSE and PIC at other layers detector, and so the new scheme is of less time delay. The scheme was evaluated by computer simulation, simulation results states the new scheme is at a litter loss of performance to ZF-VBLAST.

articleTitle: An improved music algorithm based on Lanczos process
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we present another method for DOA estimation without the necessary complete eigendecomposition, it is based on the improved Lanczos process and Sturm algorithm as well as Dichotomy method, and Finally, in the case of a Uniform Linear Array of eighteen isotropic sensors spaced a half wavelength apart with additive and uncorrelated white noise, we provide a simulated data example to evaluate the proposed method.

articleTitle: An on-demand routing protocol with cache administration in ICAR system
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Integrated cellular and ad hoc relaying system (iCAR) is a new wireless system architecture based on the combination of cellular and modern ad hoc relaying technologies. The ICAR system can balance loads of the system, increase the system's capacity cost effectively, reduce transmission power for mobile hosts and extend system coverage by using ad hoc relaying stations (ARS) to relay traffic from one cell cluster to another dynamically. Fast efficient relaying routing protocols that can exactly reflect the cell's status are important to ICAR networks. In this paper, a routing protocol designed based on on-demand routing protocol is proposed for ICAR system. We analyze the performance of the routing protocol and the impact of cache administration on the performance of the routing protocol. Some simulation results are displayed. The results show that routing cache affects the performance of the routing protocol greatly, and the protocol can provide a shortest path from a congested cell to a noncongested cell in the least time. In sum, the time delay of the call diversion is within a tolerable range. The probability of the call failure is controlled within a comparatively low standard.

articleTitle: A suboptimum low complexity receiver for serially concatenated continuous phase modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, a low complexity Serially Concatenated Continuous Phase Modulation (SCCPM) receiver based on Walsh signal space is studied. This kind of receiver just consists of two simple integrate-and-dump filters and each followed by a subinterval sampler. Compared with other SCCPM receivers of reducing the number of matched filters, implementation complexity is much lower and near- optimum error performance can be easily obtained.

articleTitle: Cross-layer scheduling with mobility and traffic information in cellular data networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, we study cross-layer scheduling in a multiuser wireless network. The key goal is to decrease the total completion time and increase the system throughput via a cross-layer design approach. Our main contribution consists of two cross-layer information based scheduling (CLIS) schemes: max-rate CLIS (MRCLIS) scheme and proportional fair CLIS (PFCLIS) scheme. The CLIS schemes combine channel fluctuation and user cross-layer information, including mobility and file size information. The MRCLIS and PFCLIS do not need substantial change in the existing system and coexist efficiently with the max-rate and proportional fair criterion respectively. Simulation results compare the MRCLIS and PFCLIS with maxrate and PF scheduling scheme respectively, which indicate our proposed scheduling scheme have good performance. We also examine the extreme cases, which utilize only either the file size information or the mobility information.

articleTitle: Robust error correction technique using time-frequency interleave LDPC product code for MC-CDMA system
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: In this paper, a robust error correction technique is developed for the Multi-Carrier Code Division Multiple Access (MC-CDMA) system to improve the quality of communication. The technique is based on Time-Frequency Interleave (TFI) Low Density Parity Check (LDPC) product code in consideration of error propagation. The conventional LDPC code is not useful for damaged symbol bit estimation when random and burst types of errors are mixed in wireless mobile communications. To improve the performance of the MC-CDMA system, TFI technique and LDPC product code in consideration of error propagation are combined. In the simulations, the performance of the MC-CDMA system is analyzed in various interference and noise environments. The effectiveness of the proposed error correction technique used for the MC-CDMA system is examined.

articleTitle: Cross-layer design for video streaming in wireless cellular networks
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Due to the inherent properties of video communication, implementation of streaming video over wireless cellular networks is a challenging task. In order to obtain the best results, it might be necessary to perform optimization using the information available across many layers. In this paper, a cross-layer approach is proposed. The bit-rate of the video stream is adapted using scalable video coding at the application layer based on channel state estimates obtained from lower layers. Simulation results evaluate the algorithm and demonstrate better performance.

articleTitle: Multicast replication using dual lookups in large packet-based switches
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: We present a scheme using dual lookups to replicate multicast packet with no loss occurring for large IP routers with as many as 128×128 output ports. We are motivated by the fact that the length of multicast destination identifier (MDI) attached to each multicast packet is inadequate to specify exactly the subset of the output ports for the ever increasing number of multicast connections to be supported. We first present our switch fabric suitable for packet-based switches in large routers, and then give the proposed scheme charactered as dual lookups and three-stage replications. Experiment results obtained by using a real terabit router called SR1880-T which has adopted the scheme are given to verify the scheme.

articleTitle: Active Queue Management for differentiated service network
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: The presented Active Queue Management (AQM) algorithms are not suitable to the DiffServ task, which may lead to serious network congestion problem. To solve the problem, this paper develops a DiffServ AQM algorithm based on nonlinear difference equations. The control algorithm takes into consideration the committed information rate and maximum allowed burst size of the marker, in addition to the number of DiffServ flows in an aggregate, round trip time, and the probability of a packet dropping at the DiffServ network. Two theorems have proposed to prevent the congestion of DiffServ networks. Observations from the system simulations are presented, and simulations were performed to validate the accuracy of the control algorithm. The simulations for two classes of DiffServ flows verify the proposed DiffServ AQM algorithms to be valid, the performance of DiffServ is largely flow-based rather than desired-aggregate-based, and the congestion of DiffServ network can be prevented by the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Improvement of pitch detection in noisy speech based on wavelet transform
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: An improved pitch detection algorithm in noisy speech based on wavelet transform is presented in this paper. The original speech signals are filtered by LPC inverse filter to obtain predictive residuals. The predictive residuals are decomposed by dyadic wavelet transform with several scales respectively. And the spatially selective noise filtration technique is applied to the decomposed signals to sharpen and enhance the glottal closure instants of voiced speech. The pitch periods are obtained from the enhanced signals. The simulations indicated that the performance of the proposed algorithm is improved considerably both for clean speeches and noisy speeches.

articleTitle: Improved macromodelings for coupled on-chip RLC interconnects
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
abstract: Two kinds of new improved macromodelings are proposed for analyzing the coupled on-chip RLC interconnects. By using the moment matching, the T and Π models are derived, which are the same as those based on the global approximations. Then the method is expanded to the coupled interconnects, and the new improved macromodelings are derived. Compared the results of the new improved macromodelings and SPICE, it is testified that the former works great faster than SPICE, and has a good accuracy.

articleTitle: Research and design of security in Multi-agent System
publicationTitle: 2006 IET International Conference on Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia Networks
